segments.source: Coordinates turn location into numbers. Multiple spatial clues can be treated as simultaneous constraints.
A point P lies on an integer grid with x,y from 0 to 7. It satisfies x+y=7 and x−y=5. It also satisfies x≥5.
A location is valid only if it satisfies every stated equation and inequality at the same time.
Which coordinate(s) can P occupy? Is the solution unique?
1. List pairs satisfying x+y=7. 2. Keep only those also satisfying x−y=5. 3. The remaining set is [(6, 1)].
A constraint problem is solved by satisfying all conditions together, not one at a time independently.

N3. Earth, Sun, seasons, and local time
Problem 636. Earth, sunlight, and local time: case 1
Earth–Sun relationships explain broad patterns such as day length and local time, but a problem should state the simplified model it expects children to use.
For this classroom model, Eastport is 1 time zone(s) east of Westport. Each zone east is one hour later. At Westport it is 11:00.
Moving east adds one hour per stated time zone; moving west subtracts. Use the given model only.
What local time is it in Eastport?
1. Time difference is +1 hour(s) because Eastport is east. 2. 11+1=12 (mod 24).
A model supports only the conclusions encoded in its rules; seasonal light does not automatically determine daily weather.
Rule-based astronomical/time-zone model; apply signed offsets or seasonal relation.

Problem 639. Earth, sunlight, and local time: case 4
Earth–Sun relationships explain broad patterns such as day length and local time, but a problem should state the simplified model it expects children to use.

Use this simplified model: Earth’s axis is tilted. In the Northern Hemisphere, days are generally longer around June than around December. Compare June and December for the same place. Cross-domain check: researchers collected 15 reports, but 4 are exact duplicate copies that add no new independent information.
Use the stated seasonal relation; do not infer daily weather from season. For the cross-domain check, independent reports = total reports − duplicate copies.
Which of the two months has the longer daylight period in this model, and can that fact alone tell us whether it will rain? Cross-domain check: how many non-duplicate reports remain?

1. Apply the stated tilt-season relation. 2. June has the longer daylight period in the Northern Hemisphere. 3. The rule contains no information about rainfall, so rainfall cannot be deduced. Cross-domain check: 15−4=11 independent reports remain.
June has longer daylight; rainfall cannot be determined from this fact alone. Cross-domain answer: 11 independent reports.

Problem 641. Reservoir stock and flow: case 1
Many geographic and civic quantities are stocks and flows: water in a reservoir, people in a city, or goods in a warehouse.
A reservoir starts with 35 water units. Each day 5 units flow in and 6 units flow out. Assume these rates stay constant for 5 days.
Stock at the end = starting stock + total inflow − total outflow. Flow is an amount per time period; stock is the amount currently stored.
How much water is stored after 5 days? Is the stock increasing or decreasing each day?
1. Daily net change=5−6=-1. 2. Over 5 days, net change=5×-1=-5. 3. End stock=35+(-5)=30.
Do not confuse a stored amount with a rate of change; conservation links them.
